sn47.6:1.1: This parable is expanded at [ja168](). See Bodhi’s notes in *Connected Discourses* for grammatical notes. | Hesiod’s *Works and Days* vv. 202–12, a Greek text of around 700 BCE, includes a short parable similar to the first part of the Sutta. There, when the little bird protests, the hawk insists that the powerful will always vanquish the weak. The Buddhist text shows, rather, that the wise triumph.
sn47.6:1.2: The quail (_sakuṇa_) is masculine in Pali, the hawk (_sakuṇagghi_) feminine.
sn47.6:1.4: The construction here is unusual; I adopt Bodhi’s idiomatic rendering. More literally, the hawk “wouldn’t have been able to do this to me, that is, in battle”. The sense is clear from below.
sn47.6:3.4: In the gradual training, sense restraint is a precondition for mindfulness meditation.
